newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish ministry eyes 5.5 pct GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish ministry eyes 5.5 pct GDP growth.

text.p: Poland's Planning Ministry (CUP) downgraged its forecast for economic growth in 1996 by half a percentage point to 5.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), it said in a quarterly report.
"It is estimated that this year GDP will grow 5.5 percent in real terms, against seven percent in 1995," CUP's report, which summed up the first three quarters of the year, said.
In August CUP had said Poland's economy would grow by about six percent this year.
"Weakening GDP growth is mainly the result of slowing industrial and construction output compared to last year and more modest argiculture output," it said.
It said that during the January-September period industrial output rose by 8.8 percent, against a nearly 12 percent rise in the first three quarters of the previous year.
It said output growth slowed because the long winter curbed demand for construction materials and because of increased competition from imports.
CUP said that despite the slowing pace of growth several positive trends occurred in the structure of Polish industry during the first three quarters of the year.
It said quality of products improved and that productivity rose by 9.8 percent in the processing sector, whose output rose by 10.9 percent during the period.
The ministry said agriculture output this year was expected to fall one percent from 1995.
It said that crop production would fall 1.5 percent from last year and livestock procution by 0.5 percent.

CUP said the trade deficit soared six-fold to $4.5 billion in the first eight months of the year as unfavourable economic climates in many of Poland's largest trading partners, such as Germany, curbed demand for Polish goods.
It expected exports to grow by about nine percent in 1996 and imports to grow by 29 percent.
Despite the large trade deficit, Poland's current account was expected to be balanced because of cash inflows from cross-border shoppers, direct and portfollio investment, the ministry said.

It said profitability for exporters grew in the first nine months of the year against the same period of 1995 as the zloty depreciated by 10.7 percent against the dollar during that period, while producer prices rose 8.2 percent.
CUP expected the unemployment rate to remain flat at September's level of 13.5 percent.
It said this year's 1.4 percent fall in the unemployment rate was likely casued by more people working in the un-taxed "grey sphere" and not drawing jobless benefits.

CUP said that in order to reach the government's 17.8 percent year-on-year inflation target in December, consumer prices would have to grow at an average of 1.09 percent per month in the fourth quarter.
It said broad money supply growth, at 4.2 percent above inflation in the first three quarters of the year, was likely to meet its 1996 growth target of 5.1 percent above inflation.
